This paper examines merging distinct stabilization methods within the framework of convex-hull-based signal recovery. We introduce two novel algorithms, named "multi-stab" and "more-stab," which integrate the linear programming approach, the previously presented "elas" (ellipsoid algorithm) method, and interior-point techniques. Our analysis demonstrates that these hybrid strategies can enhance computational efficiency and achieve superior signal recovery outcomes. Additionally, generalized versions of our methods incorporate multiple convex constraints by leveraging the computational features of the underlying algorithms. Extensive testing, including simulations and practical applications, confirms the high performance and robustness of these proposed techniques.

This study evaluates the coaddition methods employed in DESI Legacy Image Pipeline versions 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 using both stars and galaxies drawn from Y3 DR3 sources as ground truth. Our findings indicate that nonlinear combinations, specifically the median and clipped-mean, introduce inconsistencies in the point spread function (PSF) profile that vary with surface brightness, resulting in photometric biases of up to 0.1 mag and significant PSF fluctuations. In contrast, linear coaddition approaches yield stable magnitudes and smooth PSFs; consequently, these linear methods are adopted for all Y4 data released under version 2.0.0. Furthermore, applying the PSF correction derived from nonlinear stacks to Y4 imagery enhances modeling precision, a crucial advancement for maximizing scientific yield from future surveys utilizing stacked images.

Imaginary chords connected by a slit connect to form a random trajectory within a domain, which then undergoes conformal reduction to yield a random boundary traversal known as chordal SLE. This framework is underpinned by a Beurling type approach that provides a framework for understanding the relationship between imaginary surfaces and complex domains. In contrast, this paper presents a distinct surface-based formalism governing the evolution itself. Within this new approach, each infinitesimal step of the SLE path corresponds to conformally adjusting an associated surface height function, with the final derivation establishing rigorous links between our methods and existing theories.

We establish uniform temporal bounds, specifically $||\nabla u(t)||_{\infty}\leq C\,||\phi||_{\infty}\, $ (where $\phi$ represents initial data), for three-dimensional periodic incompressible Navier-Stokes equations under conditions where friction is FR. This result demonstrates direct proportionality between the maximum norm of derivatives and initial data. The proof employs techniques from stochastic control theory, involving the formulation of a value function that satisfies a nonlinear backward-Uhbeck equation (F-H-Q). By analyzing this equation's properties, we derived estimates for both the function and its spatial gradients, thereby establishing the desired bound.

Quantum verification is essential for confirming computation results when traditional error-correction methods are unaffordable. While previous coherent state-based continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) protocols prioritize efficiency and robustness over speed, the newly proposed coherent variational quantum algorithm (CVQC) protocol solves this limitation. This new framework not only retains those positive attributes but also offers exponential verification speed compared to current standards.

Cellular morphology serves as a critical indicator in diagnosing diseases and understanding biological mechanisms, making the extraction of these features a core area of cell imaging research. However, morphological extraction is frequently hindered by imaging challenges such as varying sample preparation, sample composition, and microscope types. To address these limitations, this work introduces a deep generative model capable of synthesizing cell shapes conditioned on specific characteristics, potentially replacing actual biomedical images to create a synthetic dataset. This approach eliminates the need for extensive manual annotation typically required for comprehensive training. The resulting synthesized images are used to validate a cell tracker on various real microscopy captures, demonstrating that the tracks achieve comparable accuracy to those produced using ground truth labels. Furthermore, the synthesized shapes are applied in a synthetic annotation strategy for segmentation; this method outperforms previous techniques utilizing only ground truth labels. These results confirm the utility of the model in advancing biomedical image analysis, specifically enhancing cell segmentation and tracking. Code is accessible at https://github.com/ICCVW-2021-Paper-Authors/gan-shape-generator

Building upon established concepts, this research investigates how symbolic and hierarchical knowledge influences geometric learning in artificial systems. We trained multiple reinforcement learning agents to perform complex spatial tasks and analyzed the evolution of their internal representations over time. These studies revealed that the system gradually condensed the task's spatial layout into an abstract structure resembling a graph, where stable system states corresponded to specific nodes and transition dynamics reflected the corresponding edges. Notably, the agents demonstrated a progressive increase in robustness to environmental noise, with more advanced models effectively separating dynamic graph structures from the variables driving their actions. We further examined the role of feature persistence—how long information remains stored in memory—for the agents' performance. The data indicated a direct correlation, where greater feature persistence enhanced learning speed and accuracy. These findings were reinforced by a controlled experiment in which we artificially manipulated feature persistence; the results showed that enhancing this property consistently improved performance across all tested agent types and task variations.

The Smith and Frenkel (2009) ECMC algorithm has proven highly effective for simulating isotropic and anisotropic fluids on 3D spheres, yet its application to dipolar models often results in significant dynamical slowdown. To resolve this, we introduce a Newtonian-based ECMC variant that modifies position updates by incorporating the Hessian matrix of the momentum cross-dipole interaction. This update scheme enhances sampling efficiency by enabling larger displacement steps. In the context of dipolar models, where ECMC leads to dynamical arrest and the chemical potential becomes dependent on density, our proposed algorithm successfully decouples these thermodynamic variables. Validation through bulk properties and self-diffusion coefficient calculations for dipolar fluids reveals that this method not only yields accurate thermodynamic data but also substantially improves dynamical performance.

This paper addresses limitations in public datasets for specific acoustic domains, such as environmental or home sounds, which restricts the generalizability of models trained on them. While extensive datasets exist for these contexts, others remain small, an issue previously addressed by our proposal of event-specific and shared augmentation strategies to mitigate data scarcity. In this work, we investigate how effectively these enhancement techniques transfer across different task and domain combinations, demonstrating that domain-specific improvements yield superior results over shared strategies. Furthermore, our evaluations reveal a significant disparity in method performance between environmental sound detection and audio classification tasks, indicating that no single approach universally optimizes outcomes.

This study introduces supML, a property-based approach for verifying applications such as federated learning and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) that depend on linearity and signal superposition. Superposition, often utilized in these applications, involves combining individual signals to ensure a total signal remains valid based on its components in a distributed setting where nodes only possess local information about a line of computation. To address this distributed constraint, supML extends traditional property checking by developing new versions of first-order logic property specifications. Furthermore, it introduces the superposition graph, a computational model designed to represent distributed executions and support the evaluation of these adapted properties. Evaluating supML involves introducing corresponding verification protocols for property checks and superposition graphs, followed by the use of Datalog to demonstrate the approach's validity through various use cases.

This study presents a novel signal processing methodology that integrates multiple instances of the complex Wigner-Ville distribution to formulate a signal and estimation framework. By treating the spectrogram as a complex-valued function of time and frequency, this approach enables a signal model utilizing analytic levels and distance-based definitions. We developed an associated procedure for detection and estimation, employing both a level crossing detector and a contour-based estimator. The performance of these methods was verified using the DFT-based contour estimator, with results showing strong alignment between theoretical predictions regarding bias and root mean square error, as well as agreement with previously published findings concerning bias alternative cost functions. Furthermore, the cost associated with the delay uncertainty of this new estimator was assessed using the Cramer-Rao lower bound.

This work addresses the determination of synchronization counts and the estimation of the smallest common Lyapunov exponent for general systems experiencing partial synchronization. Our methodology evaluates an Exponential Convergence Function (ECF) for each possible target subgraph. A system settles into $K$ synchronized clusters precisely when the EEF exhibits a local maximum at $K$ distinct convergence rates. Additionally, our function enables the estimation of lower bounds for the smallest shared Lyapunov exponent among inter-cluster interacting groups. validated through applications to both artificial and empirical data.

We introduce a new robust and adaptable software module designed for efficiently and accurately modeling physical systems that combine particle movement with field evolution. By leveraging the concept of action-principle discretization, the module achieves a fully symmetric integration of the equations of motion. Its versatility is demonstrated through applications to standard tests and complex scenarios, ranging from self-force calculations to general relativistic particle dynamics.

Measurement plays a pivotal role in the operation of information engines, functioning as an information conduit that enables the flow of knowledge to drive physical processes. Conventional approaches model this by representing measurement as a stochastic map converting the system's probability distribution into a new one, typically assumed to be swift and approximate as a unitary operation conditioned on the acquired data. By contrast, this study examines a continuous measurement framework rooted in the dynamics of a quantum stochastic master equation. We demonstrate that non-equilibrium flow effects induced by persistent detection introduce corrections to information power, the significance of which depends on measurement's time scale relative to the system's dynamics. Furthermore, the discussion illustrates these theoretical results through an analysis of a quantum Maxwell's demon operating on a harmonic oscillator.

We investigate disk jamming within a vertical channel, confined by a movable bottom disk and fixed top disk, investigating how varying disk weights influence this phenomenon. Employing numerical simulations, we demonstrate that increasing disk weights accelerate jamming onset. Specifically, we find channel void fraction fluctuates follow Power-law distribution with an exponent dependent on disk mass, and we derive analytical expressions linking the jamming threshold to both initial channel void fraction and oscillation frequency. We identify mass-dependent frequency thresholds defining regimes of no jamming, immediate jamming, or delayed jamming. Analytical models are developed for densities and frequencies across these states, explaining densities in non-jamming states via a balance between gravity and simulated random forces. Conversely, densities within immediately and delayed jammed states result from integrating gravity effects over sim time.

Although the traditional dipole pattern of sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies in the tropical Pacific has guided the classification of El Niño and La Niña events into distinct categories, recent research reveals significant diversity among these types. This variability in circulation anamoly structures implies differing impacts on global weather, raising critical questions regarding the specific circulation signatures linked to different El Niño and La Niña flavors that warrant further investigation. This study examines precipitation anomalies associated with each classified type across both hemispheres using daily Global Precipitation Climate Center (GPCP) data spanning 1979 to 2017. Results indicate highly similar spatial patterns between El Niño and La Niña events in South America, as well as the Pacific, Indian, and Atlantic oceans. Conversely, the central and northern tropical regions of the Pacific, the equatorial Indian Ocean, and the northern Atlantic displayed divergent patterns for the two events. Regarding extra-tropical regions, similar precipitation impacts were observed over Europe, the United States, and the polar areas of both hemispheres, whereas distinct differences emerged over the former Soviet states and parts of the former Yugoslavia. Finally, the research explores the correlation between the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) index and precipitation across the northern Atlantic basin, revealing a stronger influence during La Niña years compared to El Niño or neutral phases.

This study investigates black hole (BH) formation and the resulting mass function within the context of the LISA mission. We begin by examining high-mass BHs, specifically those exceeding 100 solar masses, formed via early structure in the universe. Our analysis covers two specific scenarios: the "heavy seed" model, involving direct collapse of early massive stars, and the "light seed" model, where accretion chains begin with smaller black holes. We demonstrate that the mass spectra derived from these heavy seed processes are significantly broader than those from light seeds. This finding is crucial for modeling the direct detection of such BHs by LISA. Subsequently, we explore additional LISA detection sources, including compact binary mergers and EMRI systems (extreme mass-ratio inspirals) arising from dark matter clumps. Our results indicate that EMRIs generated in this manner would possess far greater orbital eccentricities compared to standard EMRIs produced by conventional astrophysical processes.

While flat band-induced correlation effects are prominent in honeycomb and kagome lattices, they are typically weak or negligible in hexagonal structures. However, this study reveals that distinct, interaction-driven ground states can emerge in the hexagonal lattice. This phenomenon specifically occurs in multi-orbital contexts involving $s$-$p$ band degeneracy. By employing a Hubbard model analyzed through variational cluster mean-field theory, we identify a sequence of ground states resembling those found in other geometries—namely, $p$-wave spin liquids, antiferromagnetic orders, and a chiral broken-symmetry phase. Notably, the transition between these phases is governed by orbital physics. We further examine finite-temperature phase diagrams and investigate the material relevance of these findings by calculating electronic and magnetic dispersion bands and density of states for $f\text{-Li}_2\text{Fe}_3\text{Sn}_4$.

Although phenotypic variation in proteins is a well-documented consequence of genetic differences in DNA sequences, the specific role proteins play in creating variation across other traits remains uncertain. To address this, we conducted a comprehensive analysis linking protein sequences to phenotype-associated SNPs discovered through the Human Phenotype Annotation database and various genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Our findings indicate that while some traits show SNP dependence on specific amino acid sequences—such as height or weight—other traits remain unaffected by protein sequence variations. Notably, we observed that many SNPs influencing sequence-dependent traits also impact protein structure and function, although this overlap is not universal. Furthermore, although limited data exists, some SNPs influence a trait independently of protein sequence or structure, suggesting alternative biological mechanisms. This research establishes a clear distinction between traits mediated through changes in protein structure or function and those operating through other pathways, offering new insights into the genetic underpinnings linking proteins to diverse phenotypes.

This study introduces and examines the properties of informational entropies associated with reduced density matrices, which are constructed from the DFT electron density using a variational approach. Applied to diverse confinement models—specifically disks, rectangles, and spheres in (2+1)D, as well as (3+1)D—this framework allows for the calculation of Pauli and Coulumic entropies of order $K$, where splits of the Hilbert space occur based on spatial coordinates up to $K$. Analytical expressions are derived for infinite quantum wells ($K$) and shown that informational entropy offers a sensitive probe of Coulomb correlation effects absent in the ground-state electron density, despite being confined. A particularly striking sensitivity arises at boundaries for systems with confinement orders $K=1$, effectively encoding the position-dependent scattering length. Additionally, we explore the implications these findings have for novel gradient-based functionals, suggesting potential applications in determining optimal ionization potentials across polyatomic species.

Using data from the Gaia DR2 catalog, we identified 1,000 wide binary systems with separations ranging from 1,0000 to 30,000 AU. For these pairs, we calculated relative line-of-sight and Gaia DR2-derived proper-motion velocities, which were then combined to determine the total 3D relative velocity for each system. Our analysis revealed that employing line velocities significantly reduces velocity dispersion measurement errors, a benefit that is especially pronounced for wide binaries. By utilizing the methods described, we measured the 1D velocity dispersion across separations from 1,0000 to 30,000 AU, finding values ranging from 0.91 to 1.31 km/s. These findings were compared against theoretical predictions from direct N-body simulations, Magrie et al. (2014), as well as predictions incorporating reduced dynamical mass due to stellar population gradient effects, as modeled by Biemesderfer (2017). We further investigated the influence of random and systematic astrometric biases on the wide binaries relative to closer systems (<100000 AU). Although initial results indicated a potential overestimation of dispersion in wide binaries (≥ 1,000000 AU) by approximately 1%, subsequent corrections for total angular momentum conserved within two-body interactions raised this discrepancy to 4%. Proof structures, commonly associated with Ajtai and building on Girard's interchange of ideal and representability in multiplicative linear logic, serve to capture the computational core of proof nets. While their connective components are typically understood through the lens of linear orders, this article proposes utilizing partial orders instead. We demonstrate that, given a multiplicative proof structure based on $\omega$-directed graphs, its logical meaning corresponds precisely to the tensor product of two such graphs. This significance is reinforced by observing that the connective parts of arbitrary multiplicative proof structures can be reduced to finite representations via the component analysis established by Mullegger and Mucciaccia. Leveraging this reduction along with Mucciaccia's work on tensor products over directed graphs, this study establishes that the logical content of any multiplicative proof structure is isomorphic to the tensor product of two finite partial orders.

Although the interconnectedness of global financial markets is well-documented, understanding the specific bilateral relationships between certain pairs remains an open challenge. This study introduces a new deep learning approach designed to predict the dynamic synchronization between the price time series of any two assets. The method operates by training on a reference set of asset pairs to establish a foundation, after which it can effectively forecast the synchronization profiles for all other pairs. The models demonstrated exceptional performance in identifying whether a given pair of time series are synchronized or not, achieving near-perfect accuracy (approximately 95%) on the test reference dataset. Furthermore, when applied to predict synchronization for non-reference pairs, the approach yields meaningful and realistic results. Finally, the study explores how the previously learned synchronization maps between assets influence the effectiveness of these prediction outcomes.

We introduce a coherent vibrational mode within a Landau-Zener framework to address spin-isotope coupling in large molecules. Using numerical simulations, we show that for a fixed gap separation resulting from an adiabatic crossing, matching oscillation amitrations to the gap's oscillatory behavior can reduce transmission probabilities by up to 50%. This mechanism offers a novel spin-isotope coupling strategy for lowering adiabatic transition rates and reducing thermal reaction barriers in large molecules. Extending this approach to multi-qubit systems, we demonstrate isotope-mediated control of entanglement and its conservation. Finally, we confirm that the presented mechanism remains viable even in the presence of significant decoherence.

Online advertising is vital for the internet economy, prompting advertisers to compete aggressively for users' attention. As visual inventory expands, individual visual IDs (identifiers) have emerged as a crucial idiom feature for predicting click-through rates (CTRs) and enhancing revenue. However, directly utilizing this data is complicated by severe sparsity; even top-tier companies possess only 10% sparsity at most. To address challenges in both data sparsity and entity recognition, we propose VisualD4, a framework combining identity, group, and hierarchy visual IDs. By modeling interactions among ads, users, and these visual IDs through multiple neural networks, the system effectively aggregates information from various entities to predict CTRs. Evaluations on a large-scale dataset from an actual advertising platform demonstrate that the proposed approach substantially boosts CTR prediction accuracy compared to existing baselines.

This paper explores the cardinality constraints found within BPMN2, which define permissible counts for instance occurrences of specific activity types within a business process. These constraints can impose both lower and upper limits on how many times an activity type must be instantiated to be considered valid. The author provides a step-by-step operational semantics framework for parsed BPMN2 models that incorporates these cardinality rules. This approach ensures constrained business processes maintain soundness by making it impossible to violate the defined occurrence patterns during execution. Furthermore, the paper introduces an algorithm to determine all valid executions for constrained processes while ensuring soundness is maintained throughout this computation.

Wildfires are a major source of AOD and other pollutants that degrade visibility and harm human health. This study introduces a new physics-informed statistical AOD prediction model derived from an unsupervised statistical learning technique called empirical Bayesian factor analysis (EBA). The approach integrates fundamental understanding of aerosol dynamics with data-driven analysis. First, the model identifies the dominant patterns in daily AOD variations across the United States using EBA. Second, it establishes links between these patterns and underlying meteorological drivers, such as wind, temperature, and humidity. Third, the research evaluates the impact of wildfires on AOD by isolating their specific contribution. The results show that the identified physical patterns effectively explain over 80% of AOD variability in the U.S. The physics-informed framework successfully modeled the relationship between aerosol dynamics and weather, achieving a correlation coefficient greater than 0.7. Furthermore, by distinguishing the unique signature of wildfires, the study advances a more physics-aware capability to forecast how wildfires influence AOD.

This paper introduces a privacy-preserving framework for location-based service (LBS) queries that allows users to retrieve information about entities occupying specific locations while rigorously protecting two distinct aspects of privacy: (1) the user's precise whereabouts through differential privacy, and (ii) the potential inference of other individuals' locations by the adversary. Existing approaches typically neglect dependencies among conditionally correlated data; however, this framework explicitly models such correlations to mitigate related private information risks. Additionally, to prevent differential privacy noise from causing inference errors regarding an entity's travel routes, we developed a new risk assessment metric. Complementing this, we designed and implemented a novel index structure, the TRIP-Index, to facilitate efficient sub-second query response times. Empirical evaluations using both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm that the proposed framework effectively safeguards privacy and delivers high performance.

Functional connectivity (FC) maps, derived from neuroimaging techniques like fMRI, serve as critical clinical and research tools for understanding the brain. Despite growing clinical utility, the literature lacks a comprehensive, comparative empirical analysis of how technical and biological factors influence FC map quality. This study addresses that gap by evaluating the impact of various scan parameters and biological variables on FC data using simulated and empirical datasets. Our analysis reveals that inter-site effects on functional connectivity are more pronounced and consistent than introsite variations; these site-specific signatures are particularly prominent in lower-frequency components, which align with known biological frequencies. Furthermore, while we observed clear site effects in both correlation-based and partial correlation-based FC metrics, these effects were significantly stronger in the latter, indicating that computing partial correlations enhances the consistency of site differences. Crucially, interfocal and intrafunctional variability in partial correlation FC outweighs site effects in lower-frequency bands, suggesting high potential for using this approach to distinguish individual brains or detect group disparities in a robust, site-corrected manner.

This review examines the interplay between heat flow and concentration of measure phenomena, beginning with the classical Gaussian case and progressing through the $L^p$-curvature dimension condition, the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Bernoulli space, the discrete Gaussian model, and metric measure trees.

Code-mixing involves blending two languages, a linguistic phenomenon prevalent in various global regions but currently underrepresented in research. This paper introduces a new corpus of 150,000 instances from code-mixed texts combining Hindi and English specifically collected from Twitter. We explore how different positional encoding techniques influence the performance of both BERT and T5 when applied to our corpus. Additionally, we propose an encoding strategy leveraging a multi-token approach, which outperforms standard positional encodings in standard tasks. The authors make their updated versions of both BERT and T3, fine-tuned on the newly created Hindi-English code-mixing dataset, accessible to the research community.

The superconducting gap structure was analyzed for chemically doped disordered H$_{3}$S at pressures exceeding 195 GPa, revealing a coherent nodeless gap with only minor smearing attributable to disorder. This finding confirms the phase identified by Azad et al. (2021) in the thermodynamically stable region, contrasting with earlier beliefs that the high $T_c$ observed at lower pressures (around 250–250 GPa) resulted in nodal gaps within an unstable coexistence regime. First-principles calculations were subsequently employed to deconstruct the significant pressure-dependent isotope effect ($\alpha$) seen in H$_{3}$$S$. The study shows the effect comprises a dominant phonon contribution ($\alpha_{ph}$) of primary B$_{1g}$ mode volume oscillations against the octahedral cage, accounting for roughly 1.62, alongside electron-mediated corrections ($\alpha_{eh}$) near 0.36. While electron screening limits the isotopic scaling, its influence weakens as pressure rises. BCS-based gap evolution across different deuterium masses was simulated to validate findings, with theoretical predictions of $T_c$ closely matching experimental data for all studied samples.

Subtle variations in individual DNA sequences drive the gradual evolution of species, with average influences of these changes typically serving as reliable predictors of resulting phenotypic shifts. However, substantial sequence fluctuations over evolutionary timescales often lead to cascading interactions, where initial alterations modify the impacts of subsequent mutations. This study examines such cascading effects, termed "path dependencies," within coarse-grained models of evolving polymers and random energy landscapes. Our findings indicate that even in scenarios involving random landscapes, mutation-induced path dependencies are prevalent, with their intensity correlated to a figure we name the "phenotypic J-coupling." Additionally, we analyze how this phenomenon arises in energy landscapes resembling actual biological systems, specifically those featuring both relevant and unimportant degrees of freedom. By isolating the specific contributions of unrelevant dimensions to the phenotypic J-coupling, we gain insight into when mutations act additively and when they trigger dependencies. Ultimately, these results offer evolutionary biologists new quantitative metrics to assess how robust current genetic pathways remain as new mutations accumulate.

This study introduces a gallopping strategy utilizing a proportional derivative controller with a gallopping bird model in a 3-degree-of-freedom bipedal robot to ensure a stable walking cycle. While bipedal locomotion is inherently unstable due to dynamic effects, closed-loop control offers the stability necessary for continuous movement. Consequently, this research employs an open-loop swinging phase to reduce actuation demands, while relying on a closed-loop system during the support phase to stabilize upright posture. While previous methods typically rely on linearized models for robot dynamics, our approach employs direct numerical and graphical simulations of the gallopping bird system to generate gale postures without such linearization assumptions.

Learned descriptors have significantly improved camera pose estimation by enabling accurate pose recovery even in challenging conditions. While this paper acknowledges that training data often outperform testing datasets, especially when environmental variations include changes in season or camera height, the impact of such difficulties on pose recovery remains underexplored. We introduce a new, large-scale dataset comprising over 1.5 million images with outdoor poses recovered using standard feature detectors and optimizers. This dataset supports extensive control-study experiments and robust benchmark testing. Furthermore, our evaluations cover the same methods and algorithms used in prior work, allowing for better comparison and methodological consistency. The work ultimately aims to facilitate future benchmarking and experimental standardization in computer vision research.

Personalized federated learning (PFL) aims to adapt a global model for individual clients, enhancing its local suitability. Although various PFL strategies are under active investigation, the vast majority still rely on using labeled data, which contradicts the scenario where labels are scarce. To address learning effectively in situations with limited labeled data, this paper introduces a novel personalized semi-supervised learning framework designed for clients. This approach utilizes an unlabeled data enhancement module to enrich each client's dataset, bridging the gap between local labeled instances and label-free observations. Subsequently, a semi-supervised classifier is constructed to exploit the synergy between limited labeled information and the enhanced dataset. Crucially, the entire architecture encompasses both data and model co-distillation under a supervised learning paradigm, ensuring that insights are shared among peers with data characteristics that closely match. Extensive testing confirms that this proposed method significantly boosts the accuracy of clients facing label shortages.

We investigate the Mumford-Morita-Miller class defined by compact Riemann surfaces. Our work connects linearized vector field cohomology with the Weil-Hodge structure on the first Griffiths' group of the Jacobian. Additionally, we connect this class to the Weil pairing between specific periods and the first homology of the surface, demonstrated through the application of the Chern-Weil formula.

This study examines a Markov process operating within a domain that exhibits the exit-frozen boundary behavior. The process is assumed to be Fellerian, possessing local transition probabilities that are absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. Our primary goal is to characterize a pair of properties that, mutually implying each other, guarantee the existence of a unique quasi-stationary distribution alongside exponential decay to the associated conditional semigroup. This construction yields a class of semi-groups capable of majorizing those of various other processes of this type. Furthermore, we demonstrate the validity of a Feynman-Kac formula for these constructed semi-groups and evaluate the regularity of their associated resolvent operators.

Although graphene's high electron mobility enables electrostatic control over its equilibrium state, utilizing it as an active component in dielectric particle traps has received relatively little attention. This study investigates a non-contact dielectrophoretic trap formed by combining a graphene flap with a gold electrode. Due to the ability to shift graphene's chemical potential, both the sign and magnitude of the force acting on dielectric spheres at their stable positions can be precisely regulated. The system's dynamics are described by a conservative potential created through the interaction of the electrode and graphene. This conservative framework accurately mirrors experimental observations and accounts for observed non-linearities in charge dependence. Notably, stable trapping occurs in the equilibrium region between the two surfaces, where the conservative potential exhibits a localized minimum.

Delaying treatment within the Emergency Department (ED) frequently results in extended stays in both the ED and subsequent inpatient care. Prior research suggests that every added thirty minutes of actual treatment time is linked to slightly lower 30-day revisit and readmission rates, though these studies lacked control for patient acuity, clinical conditions, and resource availability because of small sample sizes. Leveraging comprehensive data from a single large health system covering over one million ED visits and more than five years of activity, this study examined whether expanding treatment time truly reduces revisits and readmissions while accounting for acuity, conditions, and resources. An analysis of approximately 1,000 randomly selected patients revealed that a thirty-minute increase in treatment time correlates with lower revisit and readmission probabilities, yet statistical models adjusting for initial acuity, clinical condition, and resources eliminated this apparent association. These findings indicate that while treatment time serves as a useful flow metric, its impact on downstream outcomes is likely driven by patient acuity, condition severity, and resource constraints rather than the duration itself.

This study investigates the impact of environmental characteristics on learning-based decision-making within multi-agent systems, specifically a swarm where a subset of agents must locate hidden targets within a confined region. The primary variable examined is the target difficulty distribution, ranging from uniform to highly skewed toward easy or hard tasks, while total difficulty remains constant. The results indicate that the decision-making approach adopted by the agents—whether a simple randomization policy, a uniform distribution strategy, or a difficulty-estimation based on experience—depends entirely on how difficulty is distributed. The research suggests that the optimal strategy is either one that ignores difficulty information or one that utilizes a basic feedback loop between difficulty and selection, but rarely a complex, experience-dependent dynamic selection, unless difficulty is uniformly distributed. The paper proposes this behavior results from an inherent tension: avoiding difficult tasks to preserve performance versus acquiring diverse experiences to broaden future flexibility. Furthermore, because these mechanisms are fundamentally linear, difficulty only becomes dynamically important in late stages when sufficient feedback has been gathered to inform effective difficulty-aware strategies. The study concludes that the linearity of difficulty impacts selection explains both the preference for static mechanisms in non-uniform contexts and the delayed emergence of dynamic difficulty awareness.

This study presents a novel methodology for analyzing charge-dependent correlations, specifically targeting and subtracting backgrounds tied to local charge conservation that otherwise obscure the signal of yield-dependent flow. Leveraging a specific feature of the independent particle framework, associated with charge neutrality, this approach isolates contributions arising solely from flow. The model predicts these flow-related terms with charged particles to a high degree of accuracy, even in complex environments like Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, as validated by thermally produced heterogeneous ensembles containing hadrons and partons in equilibrium with radiating charged particles. The model successfully replicates the behavior of both partonic ensemble configurations and thermal hadron production within equilibrium states.

This study investigates the predictive capabilities of machine learning models in crowdfunding by contrasting features derived from project attributes and individual project creator profiles. Analyzing a dataset of 338,539 Kickstarter projects, we examine 38 features across these two categories to forecast success. Our findings reveal that while dynamic crowd behavior features hold the strongest predictive power—outperforming static project and creator metrics—utilizing both static data types alongside signals from crowd dynamics yields significant improvements in model performance. Specifically, we developed a specialized model using Kickstarter features that achieves an Area Under the Curve (AUC) score of 0.8750.

This paper introduces a distributed strategy for training neural networks aimed at detecting network intrusions using simulated attack data. By enabling multiple organizations to cooperate on intrusion detection while safeguarding the confidentiality of their private information, this approach aligns with fundamental federated learning principles. It employs a variation of the standard federated protocol tailored for trained model aggregation and evaluation. Specifically, each organization trains an initial set of models on its local dataset, then refines these models through iterative cycles based on the performance of aggregated aggregates on aggregated labels generated by partner entities. This process continues until a terminal model is developed and deployed locally within each institution.

This paper proposes an advanced algorithm grounded in the Nested Control Lyapunov Function (NLCPF) framework, specifically designed for robots equipped with serial manipulators that perform simultaneous tasks under temporal constraints. Unlike existing NLCPF approaches which demand solving complex multivariate inequalities, our proposed Algorithm yields essential numerical variables through a straightforward closed-form solution. When integrated with the recent CP-LBFGS method for optimizing task priorities, this algorithm enhances computational efficiency, enabling real-time implementation on robotic hardware. The paper demonstrates the algorithm's efficacy through a simplified series-parallel (SP) redundant manipulator across a sequence of progressively sophisticated scenarios, ranging from basic single-task operations to executing multiple concurrent objectives within strict time limits.

The performance of modern semiconductor devices is increasingly constrained by minimal scaling limits for key components, particularly gate materials and dielectric layers. This analysis explores how selecting appropriate gate materials influences critical device parameters, specifically focusing on metal-semiconductor work function alignment and the resulting built-in electric field within the gate oxide. These material properties directly dictate key behavioral characteristics, including threshold voltage, capacitance, and mobility. To evaluate their combined effects, we conducted analyses using conventional bulk CMOS structures as well as advanced FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAA) nanosheet FETs. Our findings reveal that while work function selection can effectively compensate for interface trap density variations in bulk MOSFETs to maintain threshold voltage stability, advanced GAA and FinFET architectures exhibit significantly constrained tolerance to such discrepancies due to their complex geometries.

This study investigates the robustness of phase locking and cluster synchronization in networks composed of identical, smooth, locally asymptotically stable, and autonomous dynamical systems coupled through anti-dissipative channels. We demonstrate that if each individual oscillator possesses sufficiently small parameter variations, then either global synchronization or a specific form of cluster synchronization emerges as robust solutions for sufficiently strong coupling. Furthermore, as coupling intensity increases, the resulting synchronized states (whether global or clustered) undergo smooth transitions via anti-dissipative mechanisms. These transitions occur as the coupling passes specific critical values, causing existing synchronization manifolds to fragment into discrete clusters. The classification and description of these transitions—such as supercritical bifurcations of Hopf type or saddle-node bifurcations—are supported by numerical simulations. Contrasting this anti-dissipative regime with the dissipative one, we highlight distinct differences regarding the resulting synchrony structures and their response to bifurcations. Our findings are validated through simulations involving chaotic chaotic Lorenz and Lorenz-like systems operating within both regimes.

This study examines whether search engine results are biased toward specific online video platforms. By querying the prevalence of YouTube across major Western search engines, a consistent pattern emerged: YouTube almost always appeared in the top results, typically occupying the first, second, and third pages. Although sometimes supplemented by Vimeo, videos from other sites, such as Dailymotion, were rarely included in these search output. Research indicates that these platforms, especially YouTube, invest heavily in search engine marketing, which likely explains the recurring dominance observed. Furthermore, the findings suggest that, beyond this platform's control, users lack the ability to influence the positioning of video sites within search results. Ultimately, the study concludes that these variables contribute to YouTube effectively monopolizing the online video landscape.

As mentioned in related work \cite{Dvali:2021wqo}, the divergence in entanglement entropy arises from UV scaling factors tied to the geometry at the corner, a phenomenon illustrated effectively by the presence of a rank-1 projectors in the bulk field density matrix. Taking a step further, this study explores the influence of general monodromy defects on the angular part of the two-point function for spin-$s$ primary conformal field theories in four-dimensional bulk spacetimes ($AdS_4$). We find that defects alter the standard logarithmic divergence observed in systems without defects; this effect depends explicitly on the monodromy parameters. Additionally, our primary focus extends to computing the finite contributions to the beta function for chiral anomalies associated general monodromy defects.

Consider $K$ as $\mathbb{Q}$ or a number field, and let $L$ be the Galois cubic subfield of $K(\zeta_{13})$. The paper defines the curve $E$ as $y^2 = x^3 - 3384x - 45496$ over $L$, which possesses a generator $\mathbf{P}$ for its $K$-rational subgroup of order 13. Additionally, the text presents the main result: the closed orbit $\langle \mathbf{P}\rangle^-$ under the action of the doubling map has infinite degree over $K$. Furthermore, it is proven that no point of order 26 exists on $E$ defined over $K(\mathbf{P}\rangle^-)$. Finally, these findings are shown to resolve specific questions regarding the global 2-descent on this curve.

This study offers a detailed, local perspective on the performance of TCP-like mechanisms subject to delay fluctuations, without relying on specific implementations. Instead, it draws upon broad yet realistic principles including packetization, fair queueing, fair acknowledgment, and additive increase/additive congestion control. The work identifies three distinct operational regimes—stable, congestion, and packetization-dominant—determined by local delay characteristics. By characterizing the properties of these regimes and determining phase boundaries based on local delay, the paper provides insights applicable to both protocol enhancements and network planning.

Semisupervised Learning (SSL) faces challenges acquiring fully labeled datasets across all classes, often resulting in data scarcity that hampers model performance. To overcome this, Co-training has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing label efficiency. Current methods apply Co-training to augment pseudo-labels for standard Supervised Graph Neural Networks (GGNNs); however, these strategies neglect intrinsic graph characteristics and the common issues present in self-supervised settings, leading to suboptimal graph representations and limited label utility. To address this, we introduce PCLGG (Pseudo-Label Enhanced Co-training Graph Learning), which integrates pseudo-labels into the co-training framework while preserving graph structural signals. Specifically, our method generates diverse pseudo-labels to boost node classification, employs a graph convolutional encoder for learning robust node features, and utilizes two linked graph neural decoders that stabilize training through mutual supervision. Empirical evaluations on benchmark SSL datasets demonstrate that PCLLG consistently surpasses existing baselines, achieving a new state-of-the-art in semi-supervised node classification.

Deep models are increasingly applied to object detection in video, but the high volume of input data often leads to computational inefficiency, resulting in slower detection speeds. To address this latency, we introduce PatchNet, a lightweight architecture designed to process video frames through small patches rather than full frames. Evaluating PatchNet against leading lightweight alternatives—including MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, and Efficient-ELTNet—we demonstrate its superiority in both accuracy and speed. Specifically, Patch2 increases detection throughput by 30% to 50% (achieving up to a 70% improvement over previous models) with only minimal performance trade-offs. Notably, it outpaces other lightweight models in accuracy, delivering 10% to 20% higher performance in COCO keypoint detection and 1% to 2.5% higher in object detection. These advantages stem from its modular design, which integrates multi-scale feature extraction, specialized detection heads, and an auxiliary loss function.

We examine the discrete-time TASEP, beginning with steps derived from Beta-distributed initial conditions and deriving closed-form expressions for the $N$-point distribution using determinantal formulas. Our focus is on the regime involving large $N$ with equal short times ($t_1 = \cdots = t_N \propto L^{1/3}$), yielding the Airy-scaled multi-point distribution in the $L \to \infty$ limit. This result generalizes the findings of Borodin, Romans, and Vir\"ag (2014), who addressed the two-point case with step rates proportional to their positions. Additionally, we analyze the limits where all steps converge or all converge to infinity, showing that the air function simplifies to a two component structure in the $l$ limit. Our approach is based on extending the methodology of Borodin, Romans, and Vir\"ag, which utilizes transformations of probability distributions and connections to trigonometric and exponential random matrices.

This study investigates resource allocation strategies for simultaneous wireless-information and power transfer (SWIPT)-enabled general antenna-switching (AS) networks, addressing a technique capable of supporting both single- and multi-stream transmissions. Recognizing that the AS protocol enhances downstream energy efficiency by reducing continuous transmission duration, the research establishes maximum data rates under constraints including input power, receiver energy harvest limits, and total network power consumption. To achieve cost-effectiveness, we develop general algorithms that maximize energy efficiency by jointly optimizing transmit beamformers and antenna switching schedules, successfully flattening the efficiency gap between multi-stream and single-stream operations. Additionally, we introduce maximum-utility approaches for network operators by leveraging time-switching and time-power-splitting schemes at the user end to further boost efficiency. Simulations confirm that, within SWIPT-enabled AS networks, network energy efficiency achieves significant improvements via general antenna switching compared to AS-free networks, while the proposed wireless-enabled general AS network demonstrates superior performance against state-of-the-art networks employing transmit diversity.

Pervasive theories involving $SU(N)$ fermions play essential roles in both particle and nuclear physics. However, because these models are nonperturbative, reliable computational methods for extracting physical insights are scarce. We introduce a perturbation theory that yields the second order results for $SU(N)$ fermions, leading to the same conclusions as the large-$N$ gauge perturbation. However, the proposed perturbation differs from the large-$N$ gauge theory. Prolonged use of this perturbation method allows us to obtain the large-$N$ gauge perturbation without resorting to complex functional renormalization group equations. In addition, we present the beta function of this approach in second order and demonstrate that it converges to the large-$N$ gauge theory at high energy. Furthermore, we derive a closed form at quantum level using the present perturbation method.

This study introduces a standard classical framework for modeling electric circuit behavior in the domain of quantum electomechanics, demonstrating its applicability where quantum models can also be employed under conditions where occupation numbers are substantial. We establish an exact and precise correspondence between the conventional circuit model, the standard quantum description, and an alternative approach utilizing input-output theory. Focusing on a fundamental configuration, the stiffer cavity end-caps assembly (or similar basic resonant circuit element), we contrast these three methodologies to highlight their divergences and convergences. Our work confirms that classical and quantum treatments yield consistent outcomes regarding the dynamics of electric and mechanical modes, as well as optical field characteristics, specifically when optical modes are populated in a quantum environment. We emphasize the distinct differences in performance or behavior among pure classically and quantum approaches when dealing with low occupation numbers. We propose utilizing this classical formalism for the development of intricate circuit-based quantum devices, as it offers significant computational efficiency and ease of application compared to full quantum models. We anticipate that adopting such strategies will accelerate innovation in the engineering of complex circuit-quantum hybrid systems.

This work examines monochromic wave propagation within a fluid of incompressible, nonviscous, infinite extent under the influence of a position-dependent external field. By applying the Vortex Method, numerical simulations are performed to illustrate specific scenarios where the external field follows either an Airy or Freud's sextic weight distribution. The study elucidates the evolution of regular periodic waves and their bifurcation into steep solitary waves as the wave amplitude increases. Demonstrating that the Airy-weighted fluid supports fully nonlinear waves with harmonic profiles, the paper extends these properties to waves with rational distributions under external field forces. Furthermore, numerical results indicate the potential for the emergence of new self-accelerating solitary waves within incompressible fluids subject to the external field.

This study investigates how the limits of the field of view (FOV) in a wall-following robot equipped with a distance sensor using a single pivot joint influence its trajectory. Because the system combines nonholonomic constraints with nonlinear dynamics, an analytical solution is infeasible; thus, this paper presents a numerical approach to solve the problem. We introduce a specialized numerical method that efficiently computes the steady-state limit cycle and evaluates how trajectory errors arising from sensor FOV restrictions vary with the sensor's field of view. Our findings indicate that increasing the sensor's FOV consistently reduces these trajectory deviations. Furthermore, a surprising discovery was that a smaller FOV can induce a "scissoring" effect—a SCISSORING effect—where the resulting limit cycle's amplitude fluctuates. In perturbative algebraic quantum field theory (PAQFT), interactions and states are formulated using specific Cauchy surfaces, a necessity that creates concern given that the choice of such surfaces is generally arbitrary. We resolve this issue by reformulating the theory in terms of *double bundles* of subalgebras. Our findings demonstrate that constructing these double bundles demands fixing a background field configuration on the chosen Cauchy surface, thereby providing a plausible explanation for why semi-classical approximations require explicit background fields.

To ensure surgeon safety during operations, it is vital to detect smoke promptly, thereby preventing the accumulation of toxic gases. While existing smoke detection systems often rely on background subtraction or color-based segmentation, these methods struggle with the diverse non-smoke movements typical of surgical settings. Addressing this challenge, our research introduces a smoke detection framework leveraging the Temporal Convolutional Network (SMTC-Nets). This approach trains parallel temporal and spatial convolutional networks to identify smoke characteristics, offering robustness against surgical background noise. Validated on the public SMITE dataset, our methodology achieved over 90% accuracy, significantly surpassing conventional techniques and successfully generalizing across varying smoke densities and colors to ensure superior performance in varying surgical environments.

This study introduces a framework for developing Molmer-Sorensen gates that remain robust against frequency detargeting and are effective across all ions in a multi-ion system using solely standard Raman beams. Because the pulse shapes ensure that every ion experiences an equivalent effective Roto-n metric, the generated logical entanglement accumulates uniformly throughout the chain. The authors demonstrate this approach experimentally on a 4-ion sequence, achieving high-fidelity 2-qubit gates and successfully executing optimized 3-qubit and Clifford circuits. Additionally, the gate's performance exhibits both theoretical scalability and experimental verification for chains extending well beyond current frequency-robust implementations.

Using machine learning-driven molecular dynamics simulations, we examined how the equilibrium volume and filler A-cation size modulate off-centering effects in Ba2TiZx(PO4)3 perovskites. Our study reveals a significant scenario where the standard Goldschmidt tolerance factor fails to predict the B-cation off-axis displacement in partial-occupancy systems. Specifically, increasing the A-cation size leads to reduced off-centering for both BaPtZx(PO4)3 and (Ca0.81K0.19)TiZx(PO4)3 compositions, defying typical perovskite behavior. Furthermore, free-energy landscapes indicate that while larger A-cations expand the structural energy well associated with off-axis tilting, they simultaneously diminish the barrier separating the tilted state from the B-site displaced phase. Consequently, tilting becomes the dominant distortion over B-cation off-centering in these bulk materials under specific conditions.

GPs are frequently employed to model functions that vary across multidimensional inputs, with existing techniques such as using multiple correlated GPs, learning semiseparable covariance structures, or stacking GPs on specific variables previously proposed. In this work, we introduce a new approach that combines multiple conditionally independent GPs. This method yields a graphical model where each GP corresponds to a node, and a conditional independence relationship is visualized as an absent edge between specific pairs of nodes. We demonstrate that this graph provides an exact representation of the combined GP and further establish the equivalence between standard matrix factorization constraints and the required nonnegativity of the precision matrix's graph. Finally, finding the optimal graph involves solving multiple related multiple-choice knapsack problems.

In prior research, we demonstrated the feasibility of quantum circuits with repeating patterns for molecular calculations. This paper extends that work in two key areas. First, we find that specific recurrent circuit designs are particularly effective when the number of physical electrons is even, as they naturally incorporate certain Gaussian states. Second, and more significantly, we show that recurrent patterns are highly beneficial in quantum chemistry because the leading terms in Taylor expansions of key ground state properties—such as energy levels—against the coupling constant often contain Gaussian states. This connection proves especially advantageous for systems featuring strong correlations that resist approximation by single-determinant methods. Additionally, we show that including entanglement between single-Gaussian states within the recurrent circuit framework allows for a more direct and efficient ground state characterization.

We establish that the Generalized Chebyshev method achieves average-case superior performance compared to standard optimization algorithms, including gradient descent, when minimizing quadratically near-strongly convex quadratic-composite functions. Specifically, we provide an explicit lower bound for average-case convergence via gradient descent as well as an upper bound demonstrated by the generalized method. Our results rely heavily on recent advancements in the analysis of optimization methods under the framework of average-case convergence.

Moiré heterostructures have emerged as a focal point of research due to their capacity to create exotic many-body states. This study employs a theoretical framework based on band-structure-derived band-bond orbital models, explicitly incorporating interlayer interaction. We demonstrate that neglecting the interlayer bond-excitonic correlation leads to substantial distortions in optical spectra. Specifically, ignoring this interaction inaccurately predicts interlayer exciton binding energies and introduces significant errors in estimating plasma oscillation frequencies and their associated damping. Consequently, a proper accounting of these effects is crucial for achieving precise optical characterization in these systems.

This paper introduces a probabilistic Data Association Algorithm (PDA) that adaptively estimates the location of a highly mobile agent using a hybrid sensor array, specifically combining LiDAR and Radar. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the algorithm's sensitivity based on the magnitude of the position estimate's covariance. A probabilistic motion model, integrated with the hybrid sensor fusion, supports this adaptation. The algorithm's validity was assessed through simulation, comparing the traditional PDA with this proposed adaptive variant. The simulation framework involved generating random, randomized trajectories for the mobile agent and utilizing a corresponding random sensor array for detection. The results demonstrate that the adaptive PDA significantly enhances position estimation accuracy, particularly under high-mobity conditions where the standard PDA performs suboptimally.

Using a collected dataset of 370 pb$^{-1}$ from the DELPHI experiment at the LEP collider, the first measurement of the inclusive $q\bar q\to\ell\nu_\ell$ and $q\bar q\to\ell\ell$ processes has been performed for $e^+e^-\to q\bar q$ annihilation, utilizing $W^\pm$ and $Z$ boson polarization as the analytical tool. Within the framework of helicity amplitudes, the polarization parameters $\rho_\pm$ and $\rho_0$ were measured directly. The resulting joint helixity fractions for the $W^\pm$ and $Z$ boson polarization states were calculated as $f_L(W^\pm)=0.30\pm0.04$, $f_R(W^\pm)=0.13\pm0.03$, $f_L(Z)=0.17\pm0.02$, and $f_L(Z)=0.17\pm0.02$ (the final two representing the same fraction due to the symmetric nature of the measurement). These $f_L$ values align with Standard Model predictions within uncertainties, whereas the $f_R$ value exhibits a slight deviation. This work examines gravity in three dimensions within the framework of general relativity. A key aspect involves demonstrating that a vacuum state in three-dimensional gravity is characterized by a zero Cotton tensor. Furthermore, the C Cotton-based Lagrangian is constructed and analyzed to demonstrate that its solution yields the well-established three-dimensional Einstein–Yang-Mills theory.

We establish the mutual equivalence between orthomodular spaces and orthocomplemented orthogonally complete partial orders. In return, this finding confirms that the category of orthogently closed complete partial orders is reverse to the category generated by orthomodular lattices and orthomodular spaces.

Generated proof representations can serve multiple purposes, including search, editing, and code completion. This paper introduces the concept of using generated proofs to facilitate review processes, allowing representatives to express concerns directly over the proof structure instead of the underlying source code. We propose a large-scale language model to generate such proofs automatically and a constrained generation strategy to produce specific review formats, such as graph-based annotations or textual explanations. Our solutions effectively convey issues during reviews and enhance overall communication.

We employ Watson's formula alongside the Watson-Soundararajan-Harper techniques to compute, on average across fundamental discriminants with $|d|\leq T$, the fourth, sixth, and the general $2k$-th moments of shifted $L$-functions $L(s,\chi_d)$ for large $T$. Using this approach yields an explicit formula of the form $C_d^{(k)} T^{k}+R^{(k)}_{\textbf{i}}$, where the leading coefficient depends explicitly and non-vanishingly, and the remainder term is sharply bounded.

Over the past few decades, various generalizations of interior point methods (IPMs) for solving general conic optimization problems have been developed, with many of these approaches relying heavily on the concept of central paths and their efficient computation requiring frequent solutions to large-scale systems. Although system solution techniques have historically matched IPMs in being a primary source of computational cost, recent advancements in linear algebra have addressed this bottleneck. This paper demonstrates the potential for reducing linear algebra workload in large-scale IPMs through early termination of inner loop iterations. Based on the observation that convergence does not necessitate achieving full precision at every step, we show that inner loops can be prematurely halted, with subsequent iterations requiring fewer passes to reach high accuracy over time. This strategy is validated for both primal-dual potential-reduction methods and those based on neighborhood analysis.

QCD colorless components of the proton's spin are modeled using three quarks at low energies via the variable flavor number scheme (VFNS). This study introduces new contributions to the spin-dependent transition function $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$, which connects the spin structures of the gluon distribution and sea quarks within proton. Derived through higher-twist operators involving three flavors and calculated with exact one-loop precision using the method of finite parts (FFP), these contributions complete the flavor scheme. We also propose a simplified flavor-blind approach based on the variable flavor number system. Furthermore, low-order perturbative improvements are applied to the resulting transition function $A_{gq}^{(3)}(N)$ for comparison.

The AI Incident Database (https://aigovernancealliance.org/ai-incidents/) was established to catalog significant incidents involving artificial intelligence, drawing from over a year of collaborations to collect more than 100 documented cases. By providing structured cataloging and retrospective analysis, the database aims to accelerate the integration of lessons learned regarding risks and side effects into intelligent systems. Its proposed features—including search functionality, filtering, and cross-referencing specific attributes like root causes and mitigation strategies—facilitate the extraction of reusable insights. The authors anticipate this resource will benefit diverse stakeholders, such as regulators, media outlets, advocacy groups, academic researchers, and industry professionals, while also opening avenues for further investigation into the database's utility across these fields.

We propose a generalized residue based on the Einstein residue equations and demonstrate that this framework naturally preserves the Einstein residual principle. By applying this generalization, a modified non-linear differential equation is derived that merges the Einstein residual equations with nonlinear force of Yang-Mills theory maintaining gauge invariance. The model shows that the Einstein residual differential equations naturally incorporate the Einstein residual of finite momentum components into the second order differential equation of force of Yang-Mills theory preserving the natural property. Furthermore, it is proven that the generalization leads to a new type of particle which has mass and energy properties of fermion, but its second differential equation of force does not have the second spin property. Under the process of generalization, natural properties of fermion, photon and other fundamental particles are re-discovered. The derived general differential equation includes standard Yang-Mills theory as a subset, where the second spin property of force of Yang-Mills leads a large number of new particles, new forces and new fields. Furthermore, the second differential equation of force includes the second spin property of force, many new particles, new forces and new fields will appear. The second differential equation of force of Yang-Mills theory preserves the second spin property of force, many new particles, new forces and new fields will appear.

This paper introduces a novel monitoring algorithm designed to manage the coordination of multiple specification processes. It generates a specific output signal to suggest corrective actions, even conflicts or transitions are observed. Of particular interest is how it resolves discrepancies when different models conflict. It is implemented in a way to support a system where multiple requirements exist. It provides useful feedback for operators, even if process transitions cause conflicts.

Proto-Quipper-M serves as an extensive, proven semantic framework for Quipper, the primary programming language for designing quantum circuits. A central aspect of Proto-Quipper-M is its formal definition of quantum values, designed to explicitly encode quantum physical laws. This allows the language to verify that the non-cloning rule is preserved, where returning a function argument inside produces a distinct copy rather than a shared reference. The formal system, written in the proof assistant Coq and resting upon a PFML foundation.

This study introduces a finite-size scaling framework to examine transitions in random-matrix models, utilizing it to analyze both phase and critical-point variations with computationally efficient precision that exceeds traditional analytical or infinite-size limits of the same order. We validate this method by reconstructing the Ising model on a two-dimensional lattice and an eight-vertex model on the same lattice, simultaneously confirming their criticality and tracking shifts scaling behavior as they occur.

This research investigates quantum-enhanced optical phase sensing using quantum-tuned interferometry. We analyze coherent and twin-beam states alongside their squeezed and squeezed-beam counterparts within a homodyne framework. While Sagnac and Mach-Zehnder setups utilize standard squeezed and beam-squeezed states, we introduce novel coherent and twin-beam configurations to four-port mixing schemes for the first time. Our analysis of phase sensing performance reveals that two-mode squeezing provides the most significant improvement over other resources. Furthermore, we demonstrate that optimal sensing in the presence of unmodeled phase shifts is achieved via simple homodyne detection.

Multiway number partitioning serves as a generalization of the classic two-way number partitioning problem and has been utilized in solving the genome assembly problem. We introduce a new two-phase strategy for assembl ing genomes, leveraging Oebler's lower-bound-based two-phase approach. The capability to incorporate constraints from the conflict graph, which captures incompatible path pairs, significantly enhances the efficiency of the algorithm. Specifically, we present an innovative constraint selection mechanism that drastically shrinks the lower bound graph, a move proven to substantially improve performance. Using this method, we successfully assembled the *Caenorhabditis elegans* genome, consuming only 10 GB of disk space. Furthermore, our approach provides the exact optimal solution for *C. elegans*, outperforming existing benchmark results found in current scientific literature.

This paper introduces a novel delayed logistic equation designed to model cell population dynamics and achieves global convergence to a positive equilibrium. By incorporating specific biological premises, we derive this equation, which includes a new term representing the net difference between adhesive and non-adhesive growth rates. This component accounts for how cellular adhesion influences population expansion. We establish that this equation follows the structure of a $u$-superlinear, $u$-monotone, $u$-concave operator. Leveraging these properties and applying relevant theorems by Amann, we proof the existence, uniqueness, and global stability of a positive steady-state solution. Furthermore, by applying a corresponding Theorem by Wright to this equation, we demonstrate that the cell population converges globally to a non-zero limit, ensuring the establishment of a stable, positive equilibrium.

This study applies Isometric Log-Ratio (ILR) transformations to investigate the temporal dynamics of point processes, with specific focus on modeling the event times associated with the human reproductive lifecycle. By analyzing the logarithmic spacing between consecutive pregnancies, the research demonstrates how ILR transformations linearize otherwise complex, nonlinear patterns inherent in human reproduction. Findings reveal that once transformed, these event times conform effectively to linear regression models. Furthermore, the approach enhances the statistical power of analysis by drastically reducing multicollinearity among regressors and enables the meaningful aggregation of disparate categories within the independent variables. Ultimately, the methodology facilitates the interpretation of coefficients in terms of original units via back-transformation, allowing the results to be analyzed in log-spaced intervals between events.

Hybrid quantum devices integrating superconductors with various mesoscopic components are rapidly advancing toward full quantum functionality. These hybrid quantum conductors (HQC) offer promising avenues for generating entangled particles, manipulating the energy landscape within quantized states, and conditionally controlling electron transport. However, the specific contributions of different internal mechanisms to these effects remain unclear. This study introduces a model based on the two-mode approximation to examine the cooperative effects arising from the interaction between Cooper pairs and single electrons within an indium arsenide nanowire connected to two normal metal leads. Our findings indicate that while Cooper pair splitting is primarily driven by superconducting pairing, Cooper pair co-tunneling results significantly from Cooper pair entanglement. Consequently, the system supports the preparation of non-Fock states of matter, a capability expected to be valuable for future applications in quantum technology.

This article details a specialized setup employed to detect short-lived, neutron-deficient isotopes. Utilizing the $\beta$-$\gamma$-$X$-ray coincident spectroscopy method with the $\beta$-$\gamma$-$X$ coincidence system (where "X" refers to X-ray detection), the study measured several recently discovered or proposed neutron-rich nuclei. Specifically, the research successfully identified the properties of the technique's applicability for detecting long-lived neutron-deficient nuclides. The results confirm its ability to resolve overlapping peaks by leveraging the full energy of coincident $\gamma$-rays, thereby improving peak identification quality. Text biasing involves creating a biased probability distribution over certain words to recognize structured or formatted data, such as social security numbers. This study presents a biasing approach utilizing pre-linguistic representations as features for biasing over specific words within BERT models. Our experiments indicate that biasing remains highly effective even when employing pre-trained BERTs for which no annotated examples exist for either the target vocabulary or the language in use.

This study reports a measurement of top quark pair production cross sections using 39 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV, analyzed by the CMS experiment at the LHC. The full dataset was utilized to determine top quark production cross sections across multiple kinematic regimes. The resulting cross sections for top quark pair production align well with next-to-next-to-leading perturbative quantum chromodynamics predictions. Furthermore, the ratio of top quark production via top quark pairs to top quark single production has been determined, and the measured top quark single production cross section shows consistency with next-to-leading perturbative quantum chromodynamics predictions. The analysis also provides differential cross sections as functions of the top quark pairs' scalar and transverse momenta, the individual top quark momenta, charged-particle multiplicity, and the p$_T$ and eta of jets and particles within jets, alongside predicted cross sections by particle physics models.

Current SQL parsing frameworks primarily depend on hand-crafted rules or machine learning models trained on existing database records. A key limitation of these approaches is their inability to generalize to test instances with absent content, which often leads to incorrect query evaluations. To address this, we propose a framework called CoSQL that incorporates common semantic constraints into a joint probabilistic model. This allows the QAE problem to be reformulated as a constraint-driven quadratic integer programming task. Consequently, semantic parsing and instance evaluation evolve into an iterative process of semantic disambiguation and context filling. Extensive testing on the Benchmark SQL dataset shows that our method achieves a 31% improvement in exact match accuracy and a 53% improvement in exact match accuracy for specific subtasks compared to the best existing systems, demonstrating superior handling of queries where database contents are missing. Open source materials are available at https://github.com/stanford-hfg/CoSQL.
